newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures track sideways awaiting direction.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures track sideways awaiting direction.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures tracked sideways holding a narrow range on Wednesday, awaiting fresh direction from NYMEX and the API report on U.S. oil stocks due later today, traders said.
"It looks as if today could be a typical pre-API day, quiet and sideways," said Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives Limited in her daily report.
By 1145 GMT July Brent stood two cents up at $19.24 at the bottom of a narrow 10 cents range. June gas oil was 75 cents up at $172.75 a tonne stuck in the middle of a $1 trading range.
Technicals for NYMEX futures are flagging a possible retracement of Tuesdays losses, but fundamentals remain weak.
Chart patterns show that the markets downside may have been arrested although there is still no clear indication the bulls are in charge again.
However, despite the market's current technical volatility, lurking in the background is the perception that the market's fundamentals are growing consistently weaker.
"The biggest surprise was the fall in gasoline (on Tuesday) which traditionally is the strongest contract at this time of year due to the start of the driving season," Graham said.
"The feeling is production rates are currently so high that supply should easily cover demand, she added.
Neither crude oil inventories nor refinery capacity utilisation rates are expected to have declined significantly from last week's levels, brokers said on Tuesday.
